mentions.name: Automated dotfiles platform
mentions.description: A dotfiles setup that treats the development environment as a reproducible, automated project. Every configuration change is codified into scripts that create directories, handle symlinks, and document dependencies, so a new machine or person can be onboarded with a single 'git clone && ./setup.sh' (the 'Spilled Coffee Principle': back up in an afternoon after losing a laptop). The repo is organized in a Pillars, Pipelines, Vaults (P.P.V) structure that separates foundational configs, automation pipelines, and secure vaults, and it bootstraps AI-assisted development workflows using tmux, git worktrees, and AI coding assistants to run multiple tasks in parallel.
mentions.problem: Manually configured dev environments are hard to rebuild from scratch, and setup knowledge living in one person's head creates a single-person bottleneck when onboarding machines or people.
mentions.source_excerpt: Lately I’ve been heads‑down on a complete rethink of my dotfiles setup.  It’s not just a `.vimrc` collection – the goal is to treat the dev environment like any other project: reproducible from scratch, automated, and designed to scale as AI becomes a bigger part of daily work.
